newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-South Australia to tighten stamp duty laws.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-South Australia to tighten stamp duty laws.

text.p: The South Australian government said on Tuesday it would urgently amend stamp duty regulations in response to a recent Victorian Supreme Court decision which it said had the potential for massive taxation avoidance.

Treasurer Stephen Baker said in a statement the Victorian court decision meant opportunist parties conveying property could artificially depress its value by entering into a long term lease involving only nominal rent.

He said the court found the Commissioner of State Revenue was required to take into account the effect of a lease which substantially reduced property value when calculating stamp duty chargeable on the transfer of that property.
"The result was a significant reduction of the stamp duty which would otherwise have been payable," he said.
Baker said the SA government would give the State authority the power to disregard any arrangement, entered into from Tuesday, which artificially depressed the value of property.
The same course of action had been taken by the Western Australian government and other State Governments were believed to be considering similar moves, he said.
